page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a High Performance family server featuring an AMD EPYC processor with x86_64 architecture. It is configured with 4 shared vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a 16 MB L3 cache. Local storage is bundled with a 180 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate average performance for standard computational tasks but highlight limitations in memory-intensive operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 2306.16 and 9232.12 respectively, placing them in the average tier. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is poor, measuring 17.9 GB/sec for read operations and 12.56 GB/sec for write operations. Passmark CPU encryption tests achieved an average score of 3693.88, while the overall Passmark CPU score of 6343.77 and database operations score of 919.74 are categorized as weak and poor respectively.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and lower memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2, this server offers a budget-friendly hardware profile for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads or high memory bandwidth. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic file processing, and development environments. However, it is less optimal for high-throughput database operations or memory-bound tasks, as reflected in its poor static web serving throughput of 2.66 GB/sec and weak Redis SET performance of 3.94 million operations per second.
